title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 44 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: drones & air autonomy and space.

stories.h: Ukraine urges US to speed up interceptor deliveries as Russia targets power grid
stories.what: Ukraine's foreign minister urged Secretary of State Marco Rubio to accelerate deliveries of interceptors as Russia attempts to break Ukranian morale ahead of its winter months.
stories.you: Missile defense is one of the biggest budget lines this decade, and its software and sensors are open to newcomers.

stories.h: Ukraine firm Fire Point hopes for extension of Starshield coverage beyond Ukraine’s borders
stories.what: “If we had the possibility to expand Starshield licenses, not just on the temporarily occupied territories, but also a little bit further, like 200 to 300 kilometers, [that] could dramatically impact how Ukraine fights [Russia’s] ballistic attacks on…
stories.you: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

stories.h: Israel’s Rafael unveils new, larger cruise missile dubbed Super Ice
stories.what: Super Ice is comparable in size to the US-made Tomahawk missile.
stories.you: Weapons stockpiles are short, so anyone who can make missiles and rocket motors faster and cheaper has buyers.

stories.h: Romanian servers targeted by Russian hackers to scoop up emails about NATO, EU
stories.what: Hackers linked to Russia's FSB quietly compromised a Romanian government organization’s servers to collect emails related to NATO and the EU in December 2025, a Slovak cybersecurity firm has revealed.
stories.you: State hackers are still inside critical networks, which keeps defensive and offensive cyber in demand.

stories.h: U.K. minister drives missile-armed STARK drone boat in Oslo
stories.what: British Defence Minister Luke Pollard took the controls of STARK’s Vanta 12, a 12-meter (39-foot) uncrewed boat armed with Sea Venom anti-ship missiles, during a demonstration in Oslo this week, according to a company release sent to The Defence Blog.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

watch.h: Stopgap funding expires: FY27 appropriations or another CR
watch.why: December 11. Decides whether DAWG's $54.6B and Golden Dome's growth become real money.

idea.why: Tracks inventory, firmware, battery health, losses and operator training for thousands of drones from many vendors. Drone Dominance buys from 11+ vendors and nobody manages the mixed fleet. At 200k units, logistics is the bottleneck.
